Re-timing the drifting analog picks of catalog v4.1 (D-B072)

Written by scripts/w01_report.py from tables/ and corrections.csv.gz. Output directory /wd1/mdenolle_data/tomo_v1/checks/pick_retiming.

Summary

  • Verified on pnwstore (v01_verify.py, 12 station-days, 306 probe samples matched exactly by 101 raw counts): the picker's day trace and a short read give the same samples different times; on TDL 2014-07-13 the difference grows from 0.010 s at 00:30 to 0.521 s at 23:30 (UO HUO 2014-07-13: 0.839 s); it restarts at 0 after each data gap (TDL 2014-03-06, STD 2014-03-14, IRO 2014-03-18). A short read starts at the header time of its first record (max |deviation| 0.24 µs); inside a ~40 s short read the count drifts from later headers by at most 5.0 ms, so each pick is timed from its own record header.
  • Header scan (s01_header_scan.py, s02_scan_summary.py): 37,671 of 306,684 station-days with v4.1 picks (656 of 681 stations; NC/BK not in pnwstore) scanned record by record. 113 channels have days where header time and nominal-rate count differ by ≥ 5 ms (38 of them listed in D-B072). See the table in section 2.
  • Not only from 2013-10-22. The same count-versus-header error affects the analog channels before the 2013-10-22 onset, with the opposite sign and a smaller size for UW (about −0.08 s/day, broken up by data restarts every few hours, so typical errors of 0.03 s and up to ~0.2 s); UO FRIS and HUO were already at about +1.1 s/day in 2010; UW coastal/OR stations (OBC OCP OOW OSD OTR) and CC SEP, SUG, NED drift with the positive sign. Stations not in the D-B072 list drift too. All of these were re-timed with the same exact method (class found).
  • Re-timed and corrected, class found: 134,409 picks on 36,899 events, 75 stations; median |correction| 0.003 s, max 0.772 s.
  • Re-timed and corrected, class listed: 84,400 picks on 17,072 events, 36 stations; median |correction| 0.240 s, max 0.770 s.
  • Total corrected: 218,809 of 2,503,627 picks (8.74 %). Not re-timable: 45,879 picks (kept, flagged; section 4). Picks of stations outside the drifting set: unchanged, byte for byte (validation c).
  • Validation (a), catalog P pick − EarthScope AIC onset at drifting stations after the onset (n=673): median -0.264 s (MAD 0.104) → -0.010 s (MAD 0.020).

1. Verification on our pnwstore archive

For each station-day the day is read as the picker read it (pnwstore tsindex byte ranges → obspy.read → trim to the UTC day → HH>BH>EH vertical → resample(100) → merge(fill_value='interpolate')). At 24 hourly probe times (plus ±60 s around every data restart) the merged-trace sample and its 50 neighbours on each side are looked up, in raw counts, in an ObsPy read of only the records within ±20 s; the time of the matched sample in the short read minus its time in the day trace is plotted. tables/verify_samples.csv, tables/verify_days.csv, tables/verify_shortread.csv.

Notes: a gap-free UW day has 8,639,947 samples instead of 8,640,000 (99.99939 Hz); ObsPy joins every record into one trace (n_traces = n_segments from the header parse, every day). resample(100) keeps the start time and the number of samples of these 100 Hz channels (it does not move samples). CC.STD BHZ is 50 Hz, so the raw-count probe does not apply there (no drift in its headers: max 0.0 s).

2. Record-header scan of the station-channels with picks

Every MiniSEED record header of the vertical HH/BH/EH channels of each scanned station-day is parsed (start time as libmseed computes it, checked against ObsPy's get_record_information: identical); records are joined as libmseed joins them (|gap| ≤ half a sample) and the header time is compared with the segment start + samples/nominal rate. Coverage, by priority tier: UW, UO, CC: the first pick day of each station in each ISO week plus every day near 2013-10-22, 2013-11-18 and 2014-12 to 2015-02 (plus all days 2010-01-01 to 2010-04-13 from a first pass); other networks: the first pick day of each station in each month; further days as far as the run went. Scanned: 37,671 station-days of 306,684.

3. Re-timing, pick by pick

  1. Rebuild the picker's merged vertical day trace layout (same reads, trim and channel rule; ObsPy merge run on index traces, so each merged sample is known as sample q of read trace k, and fills are known).
  2. The catalog time must fall on that trace's sample grid (|fraction| < 0.001 sample): index i.
  3. Sample q → MiniSEED record r, position p (cumulative npts from the record that starts the ObsPy trace).
  4. Short read: ObsPy reads records r−3…r+3 only; the 101 raw counts around the sample must be identical at that position (and the uniqueness of the match is recorded).
  5. True time = start time of record r read alone by ObsPy + p/100 (within a ~7 s record the 99.9994 vs 100 Hz count error is < 0.05 ms). Correction = true − catalog.

No rate model is used. Picks inside a merge fill (gaps, overlaps) are timed from the nearest real sample (flag in_fill). A station-day is corrected when its channel drifts by ≥ 5 ms (scan) or any of its re-timed picks moves by ≥ 5 ms; all picks of such a day are then set to their sample's header time.

Exact re-timing versus the rate model of the UW check (0.521 s/day UW, 0.79 s/day UO from 00:00 UTC, a02_model_compare.py), listed stations inside the model epochs, n=84,400: median |difference| 5.0 ms; |difference| > 0.05 s for 3.7 % and > 0.1 s for 3.4 % of the picks (days where a data restart reset the count, and the UO seasonal rate); 12.4 % of the picks are on days with more than one segment.

1969 picks fall on merge-filled samples (interpolated across a data restart in the picker's trace); they are timed from the nearest real sample and flagged in_fill in corrections.csv. Most sit at network-wide data restarts (e.g. 2013-11-17 14:37:09), so they are probably picks of the restart itself.

Not checked here: NC and BK picks (the picker read them from NCEDC FDSN, not pnwstore); channels at rates other than 100 Hz (none drifted in the scan); station-days not scanned (see coverage).

Which time base is right? The AIC onsets are themselves timed by EarthScope record headers, so (a) only shows that the re-timed picks agree with the headers. The co-located pairs with a GPS-timed digital reference (LON BHZ, STD.CC BHZ, B202 borehole, MG05/MG06/MK08 OBS) decide it: regressing the pick difference on the correction of the analog pick (least absolute deviations, one intercept per pair and phase, bootstrap SE), the catalog difference has slope −1 and the re-timed one slope 0 if the record headers are right (0 and +1 if the sample count were right), separately for the listed and found classes. tables/validation_colocated_slope.csv:

6. Files and how to use them

  • Cascadia_picks_catalog_v4.1t.csv: the full v4.1 pick file, same columns and formatting, plus timing_corrected (True/False) and timing_correction_s. Corrected rows have the new pick_datetime and travel_time(s) = new pick − origin time of the event file (origins unchanged).
  • corrections.csv / .csv.gz: one row per re-timed pick (pick_row = 0-based data row of the v4.1 file), old/new time, correction, method, flag, record used.
  • README.md: method, numbers, use in the v5.1 relocation.

Scripts (in scripts/): prt_common.py (pnwstore index/read, MiniSEED header parser), v01_verify.py, s01_header_scan.py, s02_scan_summary.py, r00_tasks.py, r01_retime.py, r02_ext_tasks.py, r03_control_tasks.py, a01_assemble.py, v02_validate.py, f01_figs.py, w01_report.py.
